intro_html: Curried sausages are an Australian and New Zealand staple that most Americans have never heard of, which is a shame, because it is one of the cheapest good dinners there is. Whole browned sausages simmered in a curry gravy with carrots and peas, spooned over rice. It carries 34 grams of protein at about $2.56 a bowl (at everyday cost).
cost_closing_html: About $2.56 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a curry gravy dinner. The sausages are nearly the whole cost, so a sale on them is the single biggest lever you have on this recipe.
shop_smart: Any sausage works, so buy whatever is cheapest. The original recipe literally says sausages of choice. The curry gravy is doing all the flavor work, so this is not the week to buy premium links.
Curry powder is a one time purchase that lasts a year. One jar seasons many batches. Buy a decent one, keep it away from the stove heat, and replace it when it stops smelling like anything.
Frozen peas and a bag of carrots are the whole vegetable list. Both are among the cheapest produce items we track and neither one spoils on you.
Flour and broth make the gravy. No coconut milk, no curry paste, no jar of sauce. That is why this lands where it does on cost.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large deep skillet and brown the sausages whole on all sides. Take them out and set them aside once they have color.
Slice the onions, slice the carrots into coins and mince the garlic.
Cook the onions in the sausage drippings until soft, then add the garlic and the carrots.
Sprinkle the flour and the curry powder over the vegetables and stir for a full minute. Cooking the curry powder in the fat is what wakes it up, and skipping this leaves it tasting dusty.
Stream in the chicken broth while stirring so no lumps form, add the sugar, and bring the gravy to a simmer until it thickens.
Slice the browned sausages into thick coins, return them to the pan, and simmer so they soak up the gravy and finish cooking through.
Stir in the frozen peas at the very end, season with salt and black pepper, and serve it over hot rice.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty pot weight from Step 1. Divide that total by 14 and spoon the exact amount over rice in each container, counting sausage coins so the protein lands even. Every bowl comes in near 773 calories and 34 grams of protein.

steps: Brown the whole sausages in vegetable oil and set them aside.
Cook the sliced onions in the drippings, then add the garlic and sliced carrots.
Stir the flour and curry powder into the vegetables and cook for a minute.
Stream in the chicken broth with the sugar and simmer until the gravy thickens.
Slice the sausages, return them to the gravy, stir in the peas, and serve over rice.
